title: Independently check #4373's carve Schur bandwidth: an exact formula for any eliminated set, exhaustive over 196,512 layouts (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

This adds `research/carve-schur-bandwidth-census/`. It is an independent, exhaustive check of unpaidmoon's #4373: with at least `b` survivors between interiors, the boundary-order Schur complement of the carve has bandwidth at most `2b−1`. That bound is `GAUSSIAN.md`'s `O(W)`. The check also generalizes the theorem to an exact formula for **any** eliminated set.

**Claim type:** a structural lemma plus an exhaustive finite census. **No new κ.** The code is separately written and imports nothing from #4373.

## Lemma

Group the eliminated set into components, joining consecutive eliminated indices at distance at most `b`. Then the boundary-order bandwidth is

    max( max_C #{survivors in [min C − b, max C + b]} − 1 ,  max boundary distance of survivor pairs within b ).

The proof is the fill-path lemma (Rose–Tarjan). It is exact for generic entries and an upper bound for any entries.

- **#4373's theorem.** Under its separation hypothesis, each interior is its own component and touches at most `2b` survivors. So the bandwidth is at most `2b−1`, attained exactly by a two-sided interior.
- **Necessity.** Separators of `b−1` survivors give chains with bandwidth `2b−1+(k−1)(b−1)`. #4373's `b = 2` chain gives `k`, as stated.

## Evidence

- **196,512 layouts:** every eliminated subset of every path `n ≤ 15`, for `b = 1, 2, 3`. On every layout the formula equals the bandwidth of an actual Schur complement with random entries over `GF(2^61−1)`.
- **Separated layouts:** all 84,491 satisfy the `2b−1` cap, and the two-sided criterion decides sharpness exactly.
- **#4285's witness:** far entry `−1/432`, bandwidth 3 and both inverse norms `488/389`, recomputed exactly.

```text
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/carve-schur-bandwidth-census --check-only
  PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/carve-schur-bandwidth-census
  PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/carve-schur-bandwidth-census outcome=completed   (~50 s, stdlib only)
```

## Not covered

- Inverse norms in general.
- Circular cells (#4286).
- The narrow solver's window width (#4373's open question 1).
- Whether real Gaussian entries produce all possible fill. Only the upper bound matters.
